study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Fang et al., Journal of Affective Disorders, 2024
study_identification_part.si4_title: Individualized gray matter morphological abnormalities uncover two robust transdiagnostic biotypes

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The abstract explicitly states the objective to identify transdiagnostic subtypes based on individualized gray matter morphological abnormalities using normative modeling. The workflow description further clarifies the purpose and sequence of analyses (derive individual deviation maps, subtype discovery, validation, and biological characterization).
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "This study aims to unveil potential transdiagnostic subtypes based on personalized gray matter morphological abnormalities." … "First, we derived individualized deviation maps (individualized gray matter morphological abnormalities) using normative modeling and used them to determine transdiagnostic subtypes … The workflow of this study is shown in Fig. 1."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: For the NEW normative model built per dataset, eligibility and QC/exclusion criteria for healthy controls are described across datasets. Discovery (CNP) specifies inclusion criteria (education, no significant medical illness, negative drug screens) and HC exclusions; COBRE and DIRECT specify diagnostic procedures for patients/HCs and exclusion due to poor image quality/missing data. Final sample sizes are reported in Supplementary Table S1.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: Discovery (CNP): "Inclusion criteria … minimum of eight years of formal education, absence of significant medical illness, and negative urinalysis … HCs had no lifetime diagnoses of psychotic/mental disorders or substance abuse. Participants with missing behavioral scores/images or signal dropouts in the cerebellum were excluded"; COBRE: "… after excluding participants with poor image quality or missing data … Patients met diagnostic criteria … HCs were evaluated …"; DIRECT site 20: "Patients … assessed … using the Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV … HCs did not meet DSM-IV criteria … Exclusion criteria for all participants included …"; Table S1 reports n per group.

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age and sex are modeled as covariates in the Gaussian process regression when estimating normative ranges. Subsequent group comparisons include sex, age, and TIV as covariates. The datasets used are single-site per dataset, so site effects handling is not applicable.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "… trained a Gaussian process regression model to estimate the normative range of regional gray matter volumes (GMVs) based on age and sex in HCs." … "two-sample t-test, with sex, age, and total intracranial volume (TIV) as covariates."

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: Data sources for the healthy reference cohorts are specified for each dataset: CNP (OpenfMRI), COBRE (public URL provided), and DIRECT site 20 (consortium described), with citations.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "The discovery dataset was obtained from the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) … and is available on the public database OpenfMRI"; "Validation dataset 1 was obtained from the Center for Biomedical Research Excellence (COBRE), accessible at http://fcon_1000.projects.nitrc.org/indi/retro/cobre.html"; "Validation dataset 2 was obtained from site 20 of the Depression Imaging Research Consortium (DIRECT) …"

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing software (CAT12) and steps (standard CAT12 VBM pipeline, 6-mm smoothing) are described. Quality control/exclusion based on image quality/missing data is reported.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: "The T1-weighted anatomical images underwent preprocessing using the CAT12 toolbox … We followed the recommended pipeline … Subsequently … smoothing using a 6-mm full width at half maximum Gaussian kernel. Total intracranial volume (TIV) was also recorded …" and "… after excluding participants with poor image quality or missing data"; "Participants with missing behavioral scores/images or signal dropouts in the cerebellum were excluded".

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The normative model is described as trained on HCs to produce z-scores for patients, but no hold-out, cross-validation, or other internal validation of the normative model is reported.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: No mention of hold-out, K-fold, or LOOCV for the normative model; only description of training on HCs and applying to patients.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.location: Fang2024.pdf.md:84-86 (methods description); no additional validation text found

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: Although subtypes were generalized to independent datasets, there is no indication that a single normative model trained on one healthy cohort was applied to an independent external healthy cohort. Instead, datasets appear to be processed separately with their own HCs.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "Reproducibility and generalizability analyses demonstrated that these subtypes could be generalized to new patients and even to new disorders in the validation datasets." (no statement about applying the same normative model to external HCs).

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The type of statistical model is specified as Gaussian process regression with age and sex as covariates, and z-scores are computed. However, key model settings (e.g., kernel type, hyperparameters) and implementation software/libraries are not specified.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: "… trained a Gaussian process regression model to estimate the normative range … based on age and sex in HCs … Z scores … were calculated to quantify deviations … Positive Z scores indicated higher GMVs … and vice versa."
